# WDS19, Learning Distributions Generated by One-Layer ReLU Networks

Read on 2026-10-25 by the computational-limits space session from the arXiv HTML
page of 1909.01812, through a fetch tool that paraphrases formulas: Definition 1,
Theorem 1, Corollary 1, Claim 1, Section 4 (the norm, bias and angle estimators).
The appendix proofs were not read. The author list and venue come from the
proceedings entry, the first page was not seen. Re-check against the PDF before
citing a constant.

## Claim

A rectified Gaussian, $\mathrm{ReLU}(Wz+b)$ with $z\sim N(0,I_k)$, can be learned:
its parameters, which are identifiable only through $WW^\top$ and $b$, are
estimated to Frobenius error $\varepsilon\|W\|_F^2$ from $\tilde O(1/\varepsilon^2)$ samples
when $b\ge0$.

## Method

Definition 1: the rectified Gaussian $\mathcal D(W,b)$. Claim 1: $W_1W_1^\top=W_2W_2^\top$
gives the same law, so only the Gram matrix is identifiable. Row norms and biases
come from truncated univariate Gaussian estimation (projected SGD after
Daskalakis et al.) on the samples whose coordinate is positive. Angles come from
the orthant identity $\Pr[x_i>b_i,x_j>b_j]=(\pi-\theta_{ij})/(2\pi)$ (Fact 1, Lemma 2),
with Lemmas 3 and 4 for approximate biases. Theorem 1: with
$\tilde O(\varepsilon^{-2}\ln(d/\delta))$ samples and time $\tilde O(d^2\varepsilon^{-2}\ln(d/\delta))$,
$\|\hat\Sigma-WW^\top\|_F\le\varepsilon\|W\|_F^2$ and $\|\hat b-b\|_2\le\varepsilon\|W\|_F$.
Corollary 1: total variation learning with $\tilde O(\kappa^2d^2/\varepsilon^2)$ samples.

## What they measured, and on what

Proofs, with lower bounds of $\Omega(1/\varepsilon^2)$ for parameters and $\Omega(d/\varepsilon^2)$
for total variation, and a remark linking two-layer generative models to
non-negative matrix factorization.

## Epistemic status

Proven, as stated in the parts read.

## The limitation that matters to us

The input law must be Gaussian. The orthant identity holds for spherically
symmetric inputs and fails for records with a hidden non-Gaussian direction. My
finding.

## Relationship to this project

Tool for aim 1 of milestone 2 in the computational-limits space
(`conj-blind-relu-client-inversion`): it is the route by which a seed-blind
server could learn a ReLU client up to rotation.

## What we need to consider for our work

For NGCA records the orthant estimates carry a structured error of order $1/d$
per pair, and the open question is its operator norm.
